scenarios.name: no-trigger-data
scenarios.why: RETRIEVE answers ENDDATA: 'CICS RETRIEVE' to the error queue, then 8000-TERMINATION

scenarios.name: no-request
scenarios.why: the request queue is empty: MQGET 2033 ends the loop at once

scenarios.name: one-request
scenarios.why: one request: the date reply put under syncpoint, committed by the SYNCPOINT before the next get

scenarios.name: three-requests
scenarios.why: three requests, each replied to with its own MsgId and CorrelId, one SYNCPOINT after each

scenarios.name: priority-order
scenarios.why: the higher-priority request is got first (MSGDLVSQ(PRIORITY), W3)

scenarios.name: request-too-long
scenarios.why: a 1001-byte request into a 1000-byte buffer: MQRC_TRUNCATED_MSG_FAILED (2080, MQCC_WARNING), the message stays on the queue; 'INP MQGET ERR:' to the error queue

scenarios.name: unknown-request-queue
scenarios.why: the trigger names a queue the queue manager has not: MQOPEN 2085, 'INP MQOPEN ERR' to the error queue

scenarios.name: no-reply-queue
scenarios.why: the reply queue is not defined: MQOPEN 2085, 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' to the error queue

scenarios.name: no-error-queue
scenarios.why: the error queue is not defined: its MQOPEN fails first and the error is DISPLAYed

scenarios.name: open-input-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the MQOPEN of the request queue answers 2009 (MQOPEN call 2): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: open-output-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the MQOPEN of the reply queue answers 2035 (MQOPEN call 3): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: get-request-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the first MQGET of the request queue answers 2016 (MQGET call 1): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: put-reply-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the MQPUT of the date reply answers 2051 (MQPUT call 1): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: close-input-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the input queue's MQCLOSE in 5000-CLOSE-INPUT-QUEUE answers 2009 (MQCLOSE call 1): its non-OK arm; the nested 8000-TERMINATION it PERFORMs closes the three queues and ends the task

scenarios.name: close-output-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the output queue's MQCLOSE in 5100-CLOSE-OUTPUT-QUEUE answers 2009 (MQCLOSE call 2): its non-OK arm; the nested 8000-TERMINATION it PERFORMs closes the queues again and ends the task

scenarios.name: close-error-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the error queue's MQCLOSE in 5200-CLOSE-ERROR-QUEUE answers 2009 (MQCLOSE call 3): its non-OK arm; the nested 8000-TERMINATION it PERFORMs closes the queues again and ends the task

scenarios.name: error-put-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): request-too-long's MQPUT of the error message in 9000-ERROR answers 2051 (MQPUT call 1): its non-OK arm; the nested 8000-TERMINATION it PERFORMs closes the three queues and ends the task

notes: CardDemo's MQ date inquiry (transaction CDRD, program CODATE01, app-vsam-mq): each request on the trigger's queue is answered on CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE with the ASKTIME / FORMATTIME date and time (the case's pinned clock), a SYNCPOINT after each; errors go to CARD.DEMO.ERROR. The queue manager is a stated fact ("mq": its name CSQ1 and CCSID 37 are illustrative, CardDemo fixes neither; the request, reply and error queues the program names), given alike to both sides (register W3). The task is started by the CKTI trigger monitor in production; here its START data is stated: an MQTM ("start_data", CMQTML layout) naming the request queue (W8). The MQ copybooks are GitGalaxy-written stand-ins (W1); every MQI call is an event compared on both sides with its completion and reason code, and the queues the task leaves (its normal end commits it, W5) are compared. A wait on the empty request queue ends at once with MQRC_NO_MSG_AVAILABLE (W2). A failed MQCLOSE's WHEN OTHER PERFORMs 8000-TERMINATION while it is active (a recursive PERFORM, which IBM leaves unpredictable: register C20); the oracle is GnuCOBOL's, whose nested 8000 closes the queues still marked open and ends the task (close-input-fails). A failed close of the reply or error queue is not stated: the input queue's open flag is never reset after its close, so the nested 8000 closes it again (2019), takes WHEN OTHER again and recurses until the stack runs out on both sides.
